:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Determining an Intercept of a Tangent or Normal Line to a Curve Given in Implicit Form

:question/problem:
The circle $x^2+y^2=25$ has a tangent at $(3,4)$ that meets the $y$-axis at $P$.

![Circle with the tangent through (3,4) meeting the y-axis at P.](images/3b/3b7add027c857979a54396568b0c0a6928060f97b1af2e2a6b8520bebb025ec0.png)

Implicit differentiation has been started for you:

$$
2x+2y\frac{dy}{dx}=0.
$$

Find the coordinates of $P$. Use the tangent slope in $y-4=m(x-3)$, and remember that $x=0$ on the $y$-axis.
:question/worked-solution:
Solve the given differentiated equation for the tangent slope:

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac{x}{y}.
$$

At $(3,4)$, the tangent slope is $m=-\frac{3}{4}$. The tangent line is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-4&=-\frac{3}{4}(x-3) \\
y&=-\frac{3}{4}x+\frac{25}{4}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Set $x=0$ to find its intersection with the $y$-axis. This gives $y=\frac{25}{4}$, so

$$
P=\left(0,\frac{25}{4}\right).
$$
